subject: On-prem egress checkpoints and firewall ownership — deployment ask
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <security@summitlogistics.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: network-admin@summitlogistics.com (Ethan Liu)
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress / allowlist evidence request

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare the on-prem deployment for Summit Logistics, the security team needs a concise list of requirements and example artefacts we can hand to our network ops team. Specifically:

- Exact outbound IPs (or ranges) and DNS names the control plane and runtime will use;
- Firewall rules (ports/protocols) for private endpoints and for the optional bastion;
- Expected TLS SNI/FQDNs and whether mutual TLS is supported for the control plane;
- Guidance on egress proxies / explicit HTTP proxy support; and
- A short checklist we can include in our change request to approve production traffic.

Can you provide a short runbook + any evidence pack (sample allowlist, draft firewall rules)? We need this by EOD Wednesday to hit our change window on Friday.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Information Security Manager
Summit Logistics

--------------------------------------------
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <security@summitlogistics.com>
Cc: Ethan Liu <network-admin@summitlogistics.com>, david_kim@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / allowlist evidence request

Priya — thanks for the clear ask. I attached a concise evidence pack and a proposed firewall rule draft for your networking team. High level notes first, then attachments.

Summary (short):
- Control plane (managed) egress: short list of FQDNs and ephemeral IP ranges. We provide per-region static egress CIDR blocks when customers opt for Dedicated networking; for standard private endpoints we rely on outbound NAT from your perimeter.
- Runtime (on-prem connector) egress: single outbound socket to our control plane over TLS 443. If you require IP-based allowlisting, we can provide the ASN-level static prefixes used by our egress fleet for the US region (see attachment).
- Ports: TCP 443 for control plane; optional TCP 22 for a bastion host (if you choose SSH access for troubleshooting).
- TLS: Server-side TLS with SNI to controlplane.redwood-inference.com. mTLS is available for Dedicated/private packages — we can enable certificate pinning; please indicate if you require it.
- Proxy support: Our connector supports explicit HTTP(S) proxy via env vars and mutual auth for proxying; we also support SOCKS5 in constrained environments.

Attachments included: egress_control_design_v1.pdf (summary + checklist), firewall_rules_draft.yaml (example ip/port rules).

Quick actions for your ops team (example checklist):
1) Add outbound allowlist entries for controlplane.redwood-inference.com (TLS SNI) and the four ASN-based CIDR blocks in the attachment.
2) Open outbound TCP 443 from connector+controlplane subnets to those CIDRs.
3) If you need IP pinning instead of DNS, confirm and we will provide a signed statement of the exact CIDRs and a 30-day rotation schedule.
4) For higher assurance, enable mTLS and provide the certificate signing endpoint; we will coordinate CSR exchange.

If EOD Wednesday is tight, we can prioritize a minimal packet: the single-page checklist + explicit allowlist lines — attached as v1.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
(Attachment: egress_control_design_v1.pdf)

--------------------------------------------
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <security@summitlogistics.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / allowlist evidence request

Priya — adding a few technical specifics that your netops team will want to drop directly into firewall rules (sample rules below). I also attached a draft YAML they can import into common firewall management systems.

Sample explicit allowlist entries (US region, production):
- 34.198.160.0/20  # egress pool A (control plane API endpoints)
- 52.44.64.0/19   # egress pool B (telemetry and license checks)
- 3.120.128.0/18  # egress pool C (fallback/fanout)
- 13.58.0.0/16    # egress pool D (region-adjacent)

Ports/protocols:
- outbound TCP 443 to all listed CIDRs (HTTPS with SNI controlplane.redwood-inference.com)
- optional outbound TCP 22 to a narrow ops IP range if you enable bastion (we recommend 203.0.113.25/32 as placeholder)

SNI/TLS notes:
- SNI header: controlplane.redwood-inference.com; please do not terminate TLS at your edge for control-plane session initiation unless you enable mTLS with our team.
- If you must TLS-terminate for inspection, we require a signed attestation and an allowlist of the inspection appliance IPs so the connector can recover trust.

Proxy config:
- Set HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY for connector service. Connector supports proxy auth (basic + mTLS to upstream proxies). See firewall_rules_draft.yaml for concrete examples.

I put the sample rules in firewall_rules_draft.yaml attached. If you prefer CIDR ranges per single FQDN rather than multiple prefixes, we can generate a signed certificate containing the ranges and a rotation cadence.

Thanks,
David Kim
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: firewall_rules_draft.yaml)

--------------------------------------------
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <security@summitlogistics.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress / allowlist evidence request

Hi Priya — thanks for the follow-up and to Olga + David for the quick turn. From a product/ops sign-off perspective we recommend the following minimal acceptance items before your change window: 

- Confirm you can add the four CIDR ranges listed by David for outbound TCP/443; if not, confirm whether DNS/SNI allowlisting will be used.
- Decide on TLS inspection: if you will intercept TLS, we need a one-off attestation and the inspection IPs whitelisted.
- If you require mTLS, Laura (myself) will run the CSR exchange; please confirm the target certificate authority.

Next steps:
- Priya/Ethan: confirm which approach you will take (CIDR allowlist OR SNI-based allowlist + inspection).
- If CIDR allowlist chosen: Ethan, please acknowledge and we will send a signed statement (pdf) with the ranges and a 30-day rotation plan.
- If SNI-based: Priya, confirm inspection policy and we will list the exact FQDNs and SNI values to be used.

I can be on standby during your Friday window if you want live coordination.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[END OF THREAD]
